name: Row Data Gateway
summary: A Row Data Gateway is an object for one row of a table. It has one field for each column and methods to insert, update and delete its row, and it has no business logic.

name: Barrier synchronization
summary: A barrier makes each thread of a group stop at one point until all the threads of the group arrive. Then all continue, so the work runs in phases and each phase sees the results of the last one.

name: C++
summary: C++ is a general-purpose language based on C, with static typing, classes, templates and exceptions. The standard ISO/IEC 14882 defines it, and compilers such as GCC, Clang and MSVC implement it.

name: Primitive Obsession
summary: A code smell: a domain value, such as an amount of money or a phone number, is kept in a plain number or string, so its rules are spread through the code and the compiler cannot tell it apart.

name: Gradual typing
summary: Gradual typing lets one program mix code with static types and code without them. An unknown type matches every type, and checks at the boundary catch values of the wrong type when the program runs.

name: Declarative programming
summary: Declarative programming describes the result a program must produce, such as a query, a pattern or a wanted state, and leaves the steps to an engine that decides how to compute it.

name: Use after free
summary: A use after free happens when a program uses a pointer to memory that it has already freed, so it reads or writes memory that may now belong to a different object.

name: Concurrent pipeline
summary: A concurrent pipeline is a chain of stages that run at the same time and pass values through channels. A slow stage can have several workers, and full buffers make fast stages wait.

name: Pull up method
summary: Move a method that two or more subclasses define in the same way into their common superclass, and remove the copies.

name: Factory Method pattern
summary: A base class does its work through an abstract product and gets the product from a method that subclasses override. Each subclass decides which concrete class to create.

name: Repeated Switches
summary: A code smell: the same switch or if chain on the same kind of value appears in many functions, so each added case needs an edit in each of them.

name: Static and dynamic typing
summary: Static typing finds type errors before the program runs, from the types of its expressions. Dynamic typing finds them during the run, from the type that each value carries.

name: List files in a directory
aliases: read the entries of a folder
summary: List the entries of one directory or of a whole tree in a fixed sorted order, list symbolic links without following them, and report an error for a missing directory.

name: Collapse hierarchy
summary: Merge a subclass into its superclass, or the superclass into the subclass, when the two are no longer different enough to be two classes.

name: Check whether a string is empty
summary: Check whether a string has no characters, check whether it has only white space, and know which values each language also treats as empty and which characters it calls white space.

name: Bits, bytes and bitwise operations
summary: Every value is stored as bits, grouped into bytes and words. Bitwise operators test, set, clear and shift the bits of an integer, and a byte order fixes how wide numbers become bytes.

name: Blackboard
summary: In the blackboard pattern, independent knowledge sources add partial solutions to a shared data store, and a control component selects which source runs next.

name: Event loop
summary: An event loop is one thread that takes events and callbacks from a queue and runs each one to the end. It handles many tasks without locks, if no callback blocks the loop.

name: Move statements into function
summary: When the same statements run each time a function is called, move them into the function, so that callers cannot forget them; the inverse of Move Statements to Callers.

name: Static factory method
summary: A class gives a static method that returns an instance, in place of a public constructor. The method has a name, can return a cached object, a subtype, or no object.

name: Scheduler
summary: A scheduler object decides which waiting thread uses a shared resource next. Threads call enter and done, and one policy, such as priority or first come first served, sets the order.

name: Manual memory management
summary: The program asks an allocator for a block of memory and later gives it back with an explicit call. The programmer decides when each block is freed, and the language does not check it.

name: Write a file atomically
summary: Write the new content to a temporary file in the same directory, sync it, and rename it over the target, so that a reader or a crash sees the old file or the new file, never half of one.

name: Group items by a key
aliases: group a list by a key
summary: Group a list of words by their length, with the groups in ascending order of the length and the words of each group in input order.

name: Replace magic literal
aliases: replace magic number with symbolic constant
summary: When a number or a string in the code has a meaning that the code does not say, give it a name: declare a constant, and use the name in place of the literal.

name: Service locator
summary: A class asks a known registry object for its collaborators, so it does not depend on their concrete classes, but it depends on the locator and its needs are hidden.

name: Binary number
summary: A binary number writes a value in base 2, with the digits 0 and 1. Computers store integers this way, and hexadecimal and octal are short forms of the same bits.

name: Thread confinement
summary: Thread confinement keeps mutable data reachable from one thread only. No other thread can read or write it, so the data needs no lock. Local variables, UI threads and ownership in Rust use this idea.

name: Read and write with buffers
aliases: copy a file through a buffer
summary: Copy a file through a buffered reader and a buffered writer of a given size, then flush and close the output and report each error, also the error that comes only at the flush.

name: Assertion
summary: An assertion states a condition that must be true at a point in a program. A false assertion at run time shows a bug. Contracts use assertions as preconditions, postconditions and invariants.

name: Lazy evaluation
summary: Lazy evaluation computes a value only when a program needs it, and usually stores the result for later use. It allows infinite sequences and avoids work whose result is never used.

name: Read and write JSON
summary: Parse a JSON text with the standard library, follow a path of names and indexes to one value, and write that value back as canonical JSON with no loss of integer digits.

name: Future as a design pattern
summary: A call starts slow work and returns a future at once. The caller does other work and asks the future for the value when it needs it, and it waits only if the value is not ready.

name: Master-worker
summary: In master-worker, a master splits a job into parts, gives the parts to identical workers that run at the same time, and combines their results into the final result.

name: Callback
summary: A callback is a function that one part of a program passes to another part, so that the other part can call it, now or later.

name: Remove middle man
summary: When a class does little but forward calls to an object it holds, let clients call that object directly and delete the forwarding methods; the inverse of Hide Delegate.

name: Extract superclass
summary: Make a new superclass for two classes that have features in common, and move the shared fields and methods into it.

name: Ownership and borrowing
summary: Ownership makes one part of a program responsible for releasing each value, and other code borrows the value for a limited time. Rust checks these rules at compile time.

name: Missing authorization
summary: Missing authorization happens when a program checks who the user is but not whether that user may do the action or reach the object, so a changed id or URL gives access.

name: Source code
summary: Source code is the text of a program in the form that people write, read and change. Tools turn it into tokens, a tree and then code that a machine can run.

name: Atomic operations and memory models
summary: An atomic operation reads or changes shared memory in one indivisible step. A memory model states which writes of other threads a read can see, and which orders of memory access a program can rely on.

name: Asynchronous Completion Token
summary: An asynchronous completion token is a value that a client sends with each asynchronous request and that the service returns unchanged, so the client can match each reply to its request.

name: Divergent Change
aliases: more than one reason to change
summary: A code smell: one module is changed for several unrelated reasons, so each change must work around code that belongs to a different concern.

name: Rotate a list
summary: Move the first k items of a list to its end, keep the order of the other items, and make a k that is larger than the list work.

name: Code smell
summary: A code smell is a sign in the source that is quick to see and that often points to a deeper problem in the design. It is a hint to look closer and maybe refactor, not proof of a bug.

name: Objects and messages
summary: An object is a unit of a running program that holds state, offers behavior through messages or methods, and has an identity that tells it apart from objects with equal state.

name: Don't repeat yourself
summary: Give each piece of knowledge in a system one authoritative representation, so that a change to that knowledge is made in one place.

name: Reference counting
summary: Reference counting stores in each object the number of references to it and frees the object when the number reaches zero. Objects in a cycle never reach zero.

name: UTF-8
summary: UTF-8 is the encoding that writes each Unicode scalar value as a sequence of one to four bytes. The bytes 00 to 7F are the same as ASCII, and no byte of a longer sequence is in that range.

name: Interfaces
summary: An interface is a named set of operations that a type promises to provide. Code written against it works with every type that keeps the promise.

name: AddressSanitizer
summary: AddressSanitizer (ASan) is a compiler instrumentation that stops a C or C++ program at an out-of-bounds access or a use of freed memory. It marks bad bytes in shadow memory.

name: Acceptor-Connector
summary: Acceptor-Connector puts the code that sets up a connection in an acceptor or a connector, and the code that uses the connection in a service handler.

name: You aren't gonna need it
summary: Do not build a capability for a need that you only foresee; build it when the need is real.

name: Command pattern
summary: A request becomes an object that holds the operation and its arguments. The object can be stored, queued, logged, and run later, and with a second operation it can be undone.

name: Hide delegate
summary: Give a class a method that forwards to an object it holds, so that its clients ask the class and do not reach through it to the object behind; the inverse of Remove Middle Man.

name: Split loop
summary: Split a loop that computes two things into two loops that compute one each, so that each can be understood, extracted and changed on its own; measure before you worry about the cost.

name: Observer pattern
summary: A subject keeps a list of observers and calls each of them when its state changes. The subject knows only a small callback interface, not the types of its observers.

name: Filter a list
aliases: remove items that do not match
summary: Keep the items of a list that pass a test, in their input order, and do not remove items from a list while a loop goes over it.

name: Command-query separation
summary: Every method is either a query, which returns a result and does not change the observable state, or a command, which changes the state and returns no value, but not both.

name: Structural pattern
summary: A structural pattern is a design pattern about how classes and objects are composed into larger structures. Most of them wrap one object in another and differ in what the wrapper does.

name: Command Processor
summary: A command processor receives command objects, executes them and keeps them. Because all requests pass through it, it can add services such as undo, redo, logging and scheduling.

name: Replace function with command
summary: Turn a long or complex function into an object whose fields hold the arguments and the temporary values, and whose one method runs the work.

name: Out-of-bounds read
summary: An out-of-bounds read happens when a program reads memory past the end, or before the start, of a buffer, so it returns or uses bytes that belong to other data.

name: Behavioral pattern
summary: A behavioral pattern is a design pattern about algorithms and the communication between objects. Most of them put a behaviour that varies into its own object.

name: Operator precedence
summary: Operator precedence and associativity decide how a parser groups an expression without parentheses, such as 1 + 2 * 3. Languages agree on arithmetic but differ on bitwise and logical operators.

name: Split phase
summary: Split code that does two different things in sequence into two functions, joined by an intermediate data structure, so that each phase can be read, tested and changed alone.

name: Feature Envy
summary: A code smell: a function uses the data and the functions of another module more than those of its own, so the rule it computes lives far from the data it depends on.

name: Lazy initialization
summary: Lazy initialization creates an object or computes a value the first time a caller needs it, and stores the result for later calls. It saves work that a program may never need.

name: Strategy pattern
summary: A context object holds a strategy and calls it for one step of its work. The client chooses the strategy, so that step can change without a change to the context.

name: Compare strings
summary: Compare two strings for equality and order, and avoid a compare of addresses, of UTF-16 code units or of locale rules when you want the order of the code points.

name: Memory leak
summary: A memory leak is memory that a program keeps after it can no longer use it. The memory comes back only when the process exits, so a long-running program grows until it slows down or fails.

name: Single source of truth
summary: Master each piece of data or knowledge in one place only, and make every other use read it or derive it from that place, so that copies cannot disagree.

name: Case mapping and case folding
summary: Case mapping turns text into upper, lower or title case, and case folding erases case for comparison. Both follow Unicode data, can change the length and can depend on the locale.

name: Java
summary: Java is a class-based, object-oriented language with static, strong typing and garbage collection. Programs compile to bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine.

name: NULL pointer dereference
summary: A NULL pointer dereference happens when a program uses a pointer or a reference that is NULL as if it were valid, so the program crashes or, in rare cases, uses memory at address zero.

name: Base64 encode and decode
summary: Encode bytes as Base64 text in the standard or the URL-safe alphabet of RFC 4648, and decode the text strictly, so that bad characters, white space, wrong padding and non-zero pad bits are errors.

name: Speculative Generality
summary: A code smell: code has hooks, parameters, abstract classes and special cases for needs that the program does not have, and they make the code that it does need harder to read and to change.

name: Fail fast
summary: When a problem occurs, stop and report it at once and in a visible way, instead of working around it and failing in strange ways later.

name: Replace a substring
summary: Replace each match, or only the first match, of a substring in a string with other text, and know which replace functions take a pattern and which characters of the new text have a special meaning.

name: Parse command-line arguments
summary: Turn the argument list of a program into options and file operands, with short and long options, a default value, the -- terminator and a usage error for bad input.

name: Expression problem
summary: The expression problem asks how to add both new cases and new operations to a data type without changing existing code and with static checks. Classes make one easy, pattern matching the other.

name: Set file permissions
summary: Set the mode of a file from three or four octal digits, as the chmod command does, and return the new permission bits, with the set-user-ID, set-group-ID and sticky bits.

name: Leader/Followers
summary: Leader/Followers lets a pool of threads take turns on one set of event sources. The leader waits for an event, promotes a follower to lead, and then handles the event in its own thread.

name: Move statements to callers
summary: When some callers of a function need part of its behavior to be different, move that part out of the function into each caller; the inverse of Move Statements into Function.

name: Global Data
summary: A code smell: data that any part of the program can read and change, so a reader cannot find which code changed it, and a change in one place breaks code in another.

name: Memory address
summary: A memory address is the number of a byte in memory. A value that takes several bytes lives at the address of its first byte, and pointers and references are addresses with rules on top.

name: Flyweight pattern
summary: Share one immutable object between many uses, and pass the state that differs between the uses in as arguments. A factory hands out the shared objects, so that each value has one object.

name: Structured programming
summary: Structured programming builds control flow from nested sequences, choices, loops and calls, each with one entry and one exit, so that the text of a program shows the order of its execution.

name: Encapsulation
summary: Encapsulation keeps the data of an object behind the operations that may change it, so the object can keep its invariants and change its implementation without breaking callers.

name: Read a file line by line
aliases: iterate over the lines of a file
read lines from a text file
summary: Read a UTF-8 text file one line at a time, with only the current line in memory, and report an error for a missing file or bad bytes.

name: Continuation-passing style
summary: In continuation-passing style a function does not return; it passes its result to an extra argument, the continuation, which is a function that does the rest of the computation.

name: Count word frequencies
summary: Split a text into words, change each word to lower case, count the words in a map, and return the n most frequent words, with ties in code point order.

name: Server-side request forgery
summary: Server-side request forgery happens when a server fetches a URL from outside input and does not check the destination, so an attacker can reach hosts that only the server can reach.

name: Preserve whole object
summary: Pass the whole object to a function instead of several values that the caller reads out of that object first.

name: Active Object
summary: Active Object gives an object its own thread. A proxy turns each method call into a request on a queue and returns a future, and a scheduler runs the requests on the object one at a time.

name: Sparse file
summary: A sparse file has holes: ranges that read as zero bytes but have no blocks on the disk. So its size and the space it uses differ, and a copy that reads and writes the zeros fills the holes.

name: Null reference
summary: A null reference is a reference value that refers to no object. It marks a missing value. In many languages every reference type includes it, so the type does not show if a value can be absent.

name: The match statement
summary: The match statement compares one value with a list of patterns, in order. The first pattern that fits runs its block, and it can bind parts of the value to names.

name: Scoped Locking
summary: Scoped Locking takes a lock when control enters a scope and releases it when control leaves the scope by any path, so no return or exception can leave the lock held.

name: File permissions
summary: File permissions say who can read, write or execute a file. Unix keeps nine mode bits for the owner, the group and the others, with a umask for new files. Windows uses ACLs.

name: Algorithm
summary: An algorithm is a finite list of exact steps that takes an input and gives the answer to every instance of a problem. A program is one way to write an algorithm down for a machine.

name: Type Object
summary: A type object is an instance that represents a kind of object. Each typed object refers to its type object, so new kinds are new data, not new classes.

name: Go
summary: Go is a general-purpose, compiled language with static, strong typing, garbage collection and goroutines and channels for concurrency. The gc toolchain of the go command is its main implementation.

name: Procedural programming
summary: Procedural programming organizes an imperative program as named procedures that take parameters and return results, and divides a task into steps until each step is simple.

name: Copy a file
aliases: copy a file with its permissions
summary: Copy the bytes and the permission bits of a file to a new path, replace a file at that path, and report an error when the two paths name the same file.

name: Structured logging
summary: A structured log writes each event as a record with a level, a message and named fields, such as JSON or key=value pairs, so that a program can filter and search the log.

name: Tokens and lexing
summary: A lexer turns the characters of source text into tokens such as names, keywords, literals and operators. Its rules decide the longest match, comments, line breaks and indentation.

name: Runtime reflection
summary: The ability of a running program to examine its own structure, such as the type of a value, its fields and its methods, and to use them by name.

name: Block
summary: A block is a group of statements that the language treats as one statement. In most languages a block is also a scope, so the names declared in it are local to it.

name: Read a binary file
aliases: read the bytes of a file
read a file into a byte array
read a file in binary mode
summary: Read the bytes of a file with no text decoding and no change to line ends or 0 bytes, and read exactly the first n bytes, with an error if the file ends first.

name: Boolean parameter
summary: A code smell: a function takes a true or false argument that selects which of two things it does, so a call such as book(customer, false) does not say what it means.

name: Balking
summary: A balking method runs its action only when the object is in the right state. In any other state it returns at once, or throws, and does not wait for the state to change.

name: Loops
summary: A code smell: a loop mixes the choice of elements, the change to each one and the collection of the result, where a pipeline of named operations would show each step on its own.

name: Hash codes
summary: A hash code is a number computed from a key that picks its bucket in a hash table. Equal keys must hash equal, keys must not change, and hashes on input need random seeds.

name: Builder pattern
summary: A separate object collects the parts of a complex object one step at a time and then makes the finished object. In languages with named and default arguments, the call itself often does this work.

name: Delta debugging
summary: Delta debugging cuts a failing input into parts and tests smaller inputs until no single part can be removed and the failure stays. It turns the minimization of a test case into a search.

name: Extension object
summary: The Extension object pattern adds interfaces to an object without changing its class. A client asks the object for an extension by its type, and it gets the extension or nothing.

name: Uniform access principle
summary: Give each service of a module one notation, so that a client cannot tell whether the value is stored or computed, and the module can change between the two without changes to its clients.

name: Encode and decode UTF-8
summary: Turn a code point into its 1 to 4 UTF-8 bytes, and turn bytes back into a code point, with a rejection of each sequence that is not well formed.

name: Program to an interface, not an implementation
summary: Write client code against the interface of a collaborator, the operations it promises, and not against one concrete class, so that the implementation can change or be replaced.

name: Model-view-controller
summary: MVC splits an interactive program into a model that holds the data and the rules, views that present the model, and controllers that turn user input into requests to the model.

name: Stack and heap
summary: Each active function call keeps its locals in a frame on the stack, which goes away at the return. Data that must outlive the call goes on the heap, where an allocator finds room for it.

name: Identifier
summary: An identifier is a name that a program gives to a variable, function, type or other entity. The lexer reads it as one token, and the rules of the language decide which characters it can hold.

name: Statements and expressions
summary: An expression has a value, and a statement does something. Languages differ in where they draw the line, such as whether assignment, if and blocks give values.

name: Resource acquisition is initialization
summary: RAII ties a resource to the lifetime of an object or a scope. The language releases the resource on every exit from the scope, also on an exception.

name: Unrestricted file upload
aliases: unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type
summary: Unrestricted file upload happens when a program accepts a file of a dangerous type and stores or serves it where the server can run it or a browser can open it as a page.

name: Encapsulate collection
summary: Stop a getter from handing out the collection that an object owns; give the object methods to add and remove elements, and return a copy or a read-only view.

name: Read-write lock
summary: A read-write lock lets many threads read shared data at the same time but gives a writer exclusive access. Its priority policy decides if waiting readers or a waiting writer go first.

name: Split variable
summary: When one variable is assigned more than once to hold different things, give each thing its own variable, and make each one a constant where the language allows it.

name: Unit testing
summary: A unit test runs one small part of a program, such as a function or a class, in isolation from the rest. It checks the result automatically and reports pass or fail in milliseconds.

name: Compute a SHA-256 hash
summary: Compute the SHA-256 digest of the UTF-8 bytes of a string, or of the bytes of a file read in chunks, and give it as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

name: Rename field
summary: Change the name of a field of a record or class, and of its accessors, so that the data says what it means; when the name is also stored or sent, rename in stages.

name: Remove duplicates from a list
summary: Remove the repeated items from a list and keep the first copy of each item in its input order, and remove records that have the same key.

name: Aspect-oriented programming
summary: Aspect-oriented programming puts a concern that cuts across many modules, such as logging or transactions, into one aspect, and a weaver applies its advice at the join points that a pointcut selects.

name: Mutable Data
summary: A code smell: data is changed in place while other code still holds a reference to it, so a change in one part of the program shows up as a surprise in another.

name: Logic programming
summary: Logic programming writes a program as facts and rules in logic, and runs it by asking queries that an engine answers by unification and search, or by deriving facts until nothing changes.

name: Floating-point arithmetic
summary: A floating-point number is a binary fraction times a power of two. It covers a huge range with a fixed number of bits, but most decimal fractions, such as 0.1, have no exact form.

name: Units of measure
summary: A unit type attaches a unit, such as metres or seconds, to a number. The compiler or the library then rejects sums of different units and works out the unit of each product and quotient.

name: Execute Around
summary: An execute-around function does the setup, calls a block that its caller gives, and then always does the cleanup, so that callers cannot forget the cleanup.

name: Introduce assertion
summary: When code works only if some condition is true, state that condition with an assertion, so that readers see it and a programming error fails at once; not for checking input from outside.

name: Replace control flag with break
summary: When a loop sets a boolean variable to tell later code to stop, use break, continue or return at that point instead, and delete the variable.

name: Create a symbolic link
summary: Make a symbolic link that holds a target path, read the target back, and know that a relative target is read from the directory of the link and that a dangling link still exists.

name: Dependent and refinement types
summary: A dependent type depends on a value, such as a vector type that includes its length. A refinement type adds a predicate, such as 0 to 100. Both move checks from run time to compile time.

name: Find and replace with a regular expression
aliases: find all matches of a regex
escape a string for a regex
regex substitution with a back reference
summary: Find each date YYYY-MM-DD in a text with a regular expression, return its capture groups, and write it as DD/MM/YYYY through references to the groups, with literal separators.

name: The call stack and the heap
summary: The call stack holds a frame for each active call and frees it on return. The heap holds data that outlives its call or grows, until the program or a collector frees it.

name: Search for a substring
aliases: find the position of a substring
summary: Find the index of the first and the last match of a substring in a string, test whether a string contains a substring, and know the value that each language gives when there is no match.

name: Build a string efficiently
aliases: append to a string in a loop
summary: Build a long string from many pieces in a loop with a builder, a buffer that grows, or a list and one join, and not with a + that copies the whole result on each step.

name: Active Record
summary: An Active Record is an object that wraps one row of a table. It holds the data of the row, the code that reads and writes the row, and the domain logic on that data.

name: Design smell
summary: A design smell is a structure in the design of a program, such as a missing abstraction or a cycle between modules, that breaks a basic design principle and makes the program harder to change.

name: Check whether a string starts with a prefix
summary: Check whether a string starts with a prefix or ends with a suffix, remove a prefix or a suffix exactly once, and make the test case-insensitive without a culture-sensitive surprise.

name: Kotlin
summary: Kotlin is a statically typed language from JetBrains that combines object-oriented and functional features. One compiler turns it into JVM bytecode, JavaScript, WebAssembly and native code.

name: Long Parameter List
summary: A code smell: a function takes so many parameters that a caller cannot tell which argument is which, and a swapped pair of arguments of the same type is a bug that the compiler does not catch.

name: Message Chains
summary: A code smell: a client asks one object for another, then asks that one for a third, and so on, so the client depends on the whole path between the objects.

name: Chain of Responsibility pattern
summary: A request passes along a chain of handler objects. Each handler either handles it or passes it to the next one, so the sender does not know which object will handle it.

name: Detecting smells with tools
summary: Run linters and static analysers with rules for size, complexity, parameters and unused code, so that the signs of a smell are reported on each change and a person decides what to refactor.

name: Replace derived variable with query
summary: Replace a stored value that the code keeps in step with other data by a function that computes it from that data when asked, so that the two can never disagree.

name: Compilers and interpreters
summary: A compiler translates a program into another language before it runs. An interpreter carries out a program as it reads it. Most systems mix both, with bytecode and JIT compilers.

name: Classes and instances
summary: A class describes the fields and methods of a kind of object. An instance is one object made from it, with its own field values, sharing the methods and the class data.

name: OS command injection
summary: OS command injection happens when a program puts outside input into a command line that a shell parses, so the shell reads part of the input as more commands or options.

name: Test double
summary: A test double is an object that takes the place of a real component in a test. It has the same interface, so the code under test uses it as if it were real.

name: Consolidate conditional expression
summary: When several checks in a row give the same result, combine them into one condition with or and and, and extract it into a function whose name says the single rule that the checks make together.

name: Cross-site scripting
summary: Cross-site scripting happens when a web application puts outside input into a page without the right encoding, so the browser reads part of the input as markup or script of the site.

name: Rename variable
summary: Give a variable a name that says what it holds, and change every reference in its scope, with care for names that are shadowed and for references that a tool cannot see.

name: Rope
summary: A rope stores a long string as a tree of short pieces, so concatenation, insertion and deletion change a few nodes and do not copy the whole text. Text editors use it.

name: Context-free grammars
summary: A context-free grammar defines the syntax of a language with rules that replace a name by a sequence of names and symbols. BNF, EBNF and PEG are the notations that language definitions use.

name: Object pool
summary: A pool keeps a set of ready objects. A client acquires one, uses it and releases it, and the pool resets it for the next client, so a costly object is not created again.

name: Map over a list
aliases: apply a function to each item
apply a callback to an array
summary: Make a new list with the result of a function for each item of a list, in the same order, and know when the map runs.

name: Pull up constructor body
summary: Move the statements that the constructors of subclasses share into the constructor of the superclass, and call it with super.

name: Undefined behavior
summary: Behavior for which the standard imposes no requirements. In C and C++ it covers errors such as signed overflow, and compilers optimize on the assumption that it never happens.

name: Hello, world
summary: A hello world program prints Hello, world! and exits. It is the smallest complete program, and it shows the entry point, the standard output stream and the exit status of a language.

name: Long Function
summary: A code smell: a function does so many steps that a reader must study its body to know what it does, and the steps cannot be tested or reused one at a time.

name: Python 3.15
summary: Python 3.15 came out on 2026-10-09. It adds lazy imports, frozendict, sentinel and a profiling package, and it makes UTF-8 the default text encoding.

name: Lexical scope
summary: The scope of a declaration is the part of the program text where its name refers to it. With lexical scope, the text decides what each name means, not the calls at run time.

name: Rust
summary: Rust is a general-purpose systems language with static, strong typing and memory managed through ownership, with no garbage collector. rustc is its reference implementation.

name: Encapsulate variable
summary: Put a widely used variable behind a function that reads it and a function that updates it, so that every access goes through one place that you can change.

name: Replace parameter with query
summary: Remove a parameter whose value the function can get by itself, for example from another parameter, and let the function compute it.

name: Destructors and finalizers
summary: A destructor runs when an object's lifetime ends, at a point the program decides. A finalizer runs some time after a garbage collector finds the object unreachable, or never.

name: Short-circuit evaluation
summary: Short-circuit evaluation computes the right operand of a Boolean and or or only when the left operand does not decide the result, so a test can guard the code that follows it.

name: Marker interface
summary: A marker interface is an interface with no methods. A class implements it only to say that it has a property, and code that receives an object tests for the interface.

name: Higher-order function
summary: A higher-order function takes a function as an argument or returns a function as its result. Map, filter, fold, sort with a key, composition and callbacks are the common forms.

name: Recursion
summary: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller part of its input until it reaches a base case. Each active call needs a frame on the stack, unless a tail call is turned into a jump.

name: Ownership and borrowing
summary: Each value in Rust has one owner, and the value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope. Assignment moves a value unless its type is Copy, and a reference borrows a value without taking ownership.

name: Middle Man
summary: A code smell: a class does little but pass calls on to another object, so clients pay for an extra layer that adds no rule of its own.

name: Simple factory
summary: A simple factory is one function that takes a parameter, picks a concrete class from it and returns a new object. Callers use the object through an interface and do not name the class.

name: Mysterious Name
summary: A code smell: a function, variable, field or module has a name that does not say what it does or what it holds, so the reader must read the code behind the name to learn it.

name: Concatenative programming
summary: In concatenative programming, every word is a function from a stack to a stack, so writing two programs one after the other composes them, and no word names its arguments.

name: Mediator pattern
summary: Put the rules that join a group of objects into one object, the mediator. The objects in the group talk only to the mediator, so none of them needs a reference to the others.

name: Dependency injection
summary: An object receives its collaborators from outside, usually as constructor parameters, instead of creating them or looking them up. One place in the program chooses them.

name: Generics
summary: Generics let one definition of a function or a type work for many types. The definition takes type parameters, each use supplies type arguments, and the compiler checks the types.

name: Lazy Element
summary: A code smell: a class, a function or another program element does so little that it costs more to read and to keep than it gives, and the code is clearer without it.

name: Prototype-based programming
summary: In prototype-based programming, objects come from other objects: a new object copies a prototype or delegates to it, and a property lookup follows the chain of parents.

name: Decorator pattern
summary: A decorator wraps an object, has the same interface, and adds behaviour before or after it forwards each call. Decorators stack, so features combine at run time without a subclass for each mix.

name: Duplicated Code
summary: A code smell: the same logic appears in more than one place, so a change to the rule must be made in each copy, and a copy that is missed becomes a bug.

name: Exception
summary: An exception is an object that a program raises when an operation cannot complete. Control goes up the call stack to the nearest matching handler, and the cleanup code of each frame runs on the way.

name: Type conversion
summary: A type conversion makes a value of one type from a value of another. Some keep the value, some lose part of it, and some fail. Languages differ in which ones need no cast.

name: Insider Trading
summary: A code smell: two modules read and change each other's internal data, so neither can change without the other, and the coupling between them is hidden from the rest of the program.

name: Monitor Object
summary: Monitor Object makes an object safe for many threads. Each method holds the object's lock while it runs, and a method that cannot go on waits on a condition that releases the lock.

name: Type inference
summary: Type inference lets the compiler find static types without annotations. Local inference reads one initializer. Hindley-Milner inference solves type equations with unification.

name: Futures and promises
summary: A future is a placeholder for the result of a computation that has not finished. A promise is the side that sets the result once. Code can wait for the value, or attach the next step to it.

name: Data Clumps
summary: A code smell: the same group of values travels together through many fields and parameter lists, but the program has no type that names the group or holds the rules about it.

name: Remove subclass
summary: Replace subclasses that differ only in constant data with a field in the superclass, and remove the subclasses.

name: Embed a file in a program
aliases: include a file at compile time
summary: Put the bytes of a data file into a program when it is built, so that the program reads them from memory at run time and does not depend on the working directory or on a file next to it.

name: Extract function
summary: Move a fragment of code into a function of its own, named for what the fragment does, and replace the fragment with a call. The behaviour of the program does not change.

name: Combine functions into transform
summary: Gather the calculations of values derived from a record into one function that takes the record and returns a copy with the derived values added.

name: Move function
summary: Move a function to the class or module whose data it uses most, and leave a delegating call or nothing behind; called Move Method in the first edition of Refactoring.

name: Inheritance
summary: Inheritance defines a class as an extension of another: the subclass gets the fields and methods of its base, adds its own, overrides some, and can usually stand in for the base.

name: Type system
summary: A type system is a set of rules that gives a type to each part of a program and rejects the programs that break the rules. It finds a class of errors before or while the program runs.

name: Strategized Locking
summary: Strategized Locking makes the lock of a component a parameter, so one implementation serves single-threaded and multi-threaded use with the lock that fits each case.

name: The machine model, processor and memory
summary: A computer runs a program with a processor that fetches, decodes and executes instructions from a memory of addressed words. The program and its data share that memory.

name: Abstract Factory pattern
summary: One object has a factory method for each kind of product in a family. Client code gets all of its products from that object, so it never names a concrete class and never mixes two families.

name: Equality and identity
summary: Two values are equal when they hold the same data. Two references are identical when they point to the same object. Each language decides which of the two tests its operators make.

name: Refused Bequest
summary: A code smell: a subclass inherits methods and data that it does not use or does not want, and in the strong form it inherits an interface that it cannot honour.

name: Move field
summary: Move a field to the record or class that it belongs with, after you encapsulate it, so that data that changes together lives together.

name: git rebase
summary: A rebase replays a series of commits on top of another commit. The changes stay the same, but each replayed commit has a different parent, so it is a different commit with a different hash.

name: Inline function
summary: Replace each call of a function with the body of the function, then delete the function, when the body says what the function does as clearly as its name.

name: Conditional
summary: A conditional runs one piece of code when a condition is true and, optionally, another when it is false. The if statement and the conditional expression are its two main forms.

name: Machine code
summary: Machine code is a program as the processor runs it: instructions encoded as bytes in memory. Each family of processors has its own instruction set, so machine code for one does not run on another.

name: Mutual exclusion
summary: Mutual exclusion lets at most one thread at a time run a critical section, the code that uses a shared resource. A mutex, or lock, is the usual tool.

name: Type
summary: A type is a set of values together with the operations that are valid on them. It tells the compiler and the reader what a piece of data means, how it is stored and what a program can do with it.

name: Inline class
summary: Move all the fields and methods of a class that does too little into the class that uses it, and delete the class; the inverse of Extract Class.

name: Substitute algorithm
summary: Replace the body of a function with a clearer algorithm that gives the same results, and use the old body as the test oracle while you switch.

name: Delegation pattern
summary: An object hands a request to a helper object, its delegate, and passes itself when the delegate needs it. This gives the reuse of inheritance through composition.

name: Exposure of sensitive information
aliases: exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor
summary: Sensitive information exposure happens when a program shows data to someone who may not see it, such as a stack trace to a user, a secret in a log, or a timing difference.

name: Change the case of a string
summary: Change a string to upper case or lower case, and know when the Unicode case change of the library changes the length or depends on the locale.

name: Operator
summary: An operator is a symbol or a keyword, such as + or sizeof, that makes an expression from its operands. It is usually a short name for a function, with its own syntax and rules for grouping.

name: Count the graphemes of a string
summary: Count the extended grapheme clusters of a string, so that a letter with its combining marks, a flag and an emoji sequence each count as one.

name: Pull up field
summary: Move a field that two or more subclasses declare and use in the same way into their common superclass.

name: Measure elapsed time
summary: Measure how long a piece of work takes with a monotonic clock, not the wall clock, and print the duration in milliseconds with integer arithmetic on nanoseconds.

name: Bridge pattern
summary: Split a class that varies in two ways into two class hierarchies, an abstraction and an implementation, and join them with a reference. Each hierarchy then grows without the other.

name: Guarded suspension
summary: Guarded suspension makes a method wait until it holds a lock and its precondition is true. The thread sleeps on a condition variable and checks the guard again in a loop each time it wakes up.

name: Read a whole file
