summary: Read all of a UTF-8 file in one call and return its text with no change to line ends, a byte order mark or final newlines. Report an error for a missing file or bad bytes.

name: Replace nested conditional with guard clauses
summary: When a function nests its special cases in if and else, check each special case at the top and return at once, so that the normal case is the unindented code at the end of the function.

name: Rename a file
summary: Give a file a new name, also in another directory, with one rename call that replaces a file at the new name, so that a reader sees the old file or the new file, never a part.

name: Join a list of strings
summary: Join a list of strings into one string with a separator between each two items, and know how each language handles the empty list, items that are not strings and null items.

name: Replace exception with precheck
summary: Replace a try and catch around a call that fails in a known, expected case with a check of that case before the call.

name: Event Aggregator
summary: An event aggregator is a single source of events for many objects. It registers for the events of the source objects, and clients register only with it.

name: Encapsulate record
summary: Replace a plain record, such as a dictionary or a JSON object, with an object whose accessors are the only way to reach the data, so that the storage can change and the callers do not.

name: E0382: use of a moved value
summary: rustc reports E0382 when a program uses or borrows a variable, or assigns to a part of it, after its value has moved out, and the type of the value does not implement Copy.

name: Convention over configuration
summary: A framework decides the common cases by convention, so a developer writes configuration only for the parts of the application that differ from the convention.

name: Copy-on-write
summary: Copy-on-write shares one copy of data among its users until one of them writes. The writer makes a private copy and changes that, so readers keep a stable snapshot and need no lock.

name: Closure
summary: A closure is a function together with the variables of the scope where it was made. The function can still read and change these variables after that scope has ended.

name: Create a temporary file
summary: Make a new temporary file with a random name and the mode 0600 in one call, so that no other process can put a file or a link at the name first, then use it and remove it.

name: Thread
summary: A thread is one sequence of execution inside a process. The threads of a process share its memory, and each thread has its own stack, so several threads can run at the same time.

name: Iterate in chunks
summary: Split a list of integers into consecutive chunks of a fixed size, where the last chunk can be shorter.

name: Incorrect authorization
summary: Incorrect authorization happens when a program checks permission but the check is wrong, such as a test on the wrong object, a loose match of a role name, or a value the client controls.

name: Table Data Gateway
summary: A Table Data Gateway is one object that holds all the SQL for one table or view. Its methods find, insert, update and delete rows, and they return plain data, not domain objects.

name: Sort a list
summary: Sort a list of integers in ascending numeric order, and do not compare the numbers as text.

name: Remove flag argument
summary: Replace an argument that a caller passes only to select what a function does with one explicit function for each choice.

name: Remove dead code
summary: Delete code that no longer runs or whose results nobody uses, after you check that nothing reaches it; version control keeps the old version if you ever need it.

name: Composite pattern
summary: Leaves and containers share one interface, and a container forwards each call to its children. Client code then treats one object and a whole tree of objects in the same way.

name: Repeat a string
summary: Make a string of n copies of a string, and know what each language does with a count of 0, a negative count and a count that overflows.

name: Work queue
summary: A work queue holds tasks that several workers take and do. The queue keeps each task until a worker acknowledges it, so a task whose worker fails goes to another worker.

name: Separation of concerns
summary: Divide a program so that each part deals with one concern, and study or change each concern on its own.

name: Multi-paradigm programming
summary: A multi-paradigm language supports several paradigms, such as imperative, object-oriented and functional, so that each part of a program can use the style that fits it.

name: Count the items of each kind
summary: Count how many times each distinct item is in a list of integers, and give the counts in ascending order of the item.

name: Syntactic macros
summary: A rule that the compiler applies to program text before it gives the text a meaning. The C preprocessor works on tokens; Lisp, Scheme and Rust macros work on syntax.

name: Extract variable
summary: Give a part of a complex expression a name, by moving it into a local variable and using the variable in its place, so that the expression reads as the steps of a rule.

name: Principle of least astonishment
summary: A component should behave the way most of its users expect, so that its behaviour does not surprise them; names, defaults and conventions should match what the user already knows.

name: Proxy pattern
summary: A proxy stands in for another object and has the same interface. It controls access to the real object: it can make it on first use, check permissions, or send the call to another process.

name: Trim white space
summary: Remove the white space at the start and at the end of a string, and know which characters each language counts as white space.

name: Path traversal
summary: Path traversal happens when a program builds a file path from outside input and does not check where the path points, so `..` or an absolute path reaches files outside the intended directory.

name: Double-Checked Locking
summary: Double-Checked Locking tests a condition before it takes a lock and again after, so code that must run once takes the lock only on the first calls. The plain form needs a safe memory model.

name: SQL injection
summary: SQL injection happens when a program puts outside input into the text of an SQL statement, so the database reads part of the input as SQL code and not as a value.

name: Run a subprocess
aliases: run a program and capture its output
summary: Start a program with a list of arguments and no shell, read its standard output and standard error, and return its exit status. A missing program is an error.

name: Thread-Safe Interface
summary: Thread-Safe Interface lets only the public methods of a component take its lock, and they call private methods that never lock, so calls inside the component cannot self-deadlock.

name: TypeScript
summary: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript. A compiler checks its static, structural types and then erases them, so the program runs as JavaScript. The compiler tsc is its reference implementation.

name: Extract class
summary: Split a class that does two jobs into two classes, by moving the fields and methods of one job into a class of its own and keeping a reference to it.

name: Mixin
summary: A mixin is a class that holds methods for other classes to use, without being their parent in the sense of "is a". A class mixes in several mixins to reuse their behaviour.

name: Deep modules
summary: Prefer modules that give a lot of functionality through a simple interface; a module whose interface is almost as complex as its implementation is shallow and adds little.

name: Visitor pattern
summary: An operation on an object structure becomes a separate object with one method for each kind of element. Operations are then cheap to add, and kinds of element are expensive to add.

name: Syntax
summary: Syntax is the set of rules for the form of a program: which characters make tokens and which sequences of tokens make valid programs. What a valid program does is a question of semantics.

name: Boolean type
summary: The Boolean type has two values, true and false. Comparisons produce them, conditions consume them, and the operators and, or and not combine them.

name: Replace command with function
summary: Turn a command object that does a small job, with a constructor and one execute method, back into a plain function.

name: Parameterize function
summary: Merge two or more functions that do the same work with different literal values into one function that takes the value as a parameter.

name: Actor model
summary: The actor model builds a concurrent program from actors that each own private state and a mailbox, handle one message at a time, and interact only by sending messages.

name: String
summary: A string is a sequence of characters that holds text. Each language defines what a character is, whether a string can change, and how text differs from bytes.

name: Check whether a file exists
summary: Tell whether a path names a file, a directory, another entry, a broken link or nothing, report an error when the program cannot tell, and know that the answer can be old at once.

name: Python
summary: Python is a general-purpose language with dynamic, strong typing, automatic memory management and a large standard library. CPython is its reference implementation.

name: Thread pool
summary: A thread pool keeps a fixed set of worker threads that take tasks from a queue. The program pays for thread creation once and limits how many tasks run at the same time.

name: Currying and partial application
summary: Currying turns a function of many arguments into a chain of functions of one argument. Partial application fixes some arguments of a function and returns a function of the rest.

name: Specification
summary: A specification is an object that tells if a candidate object matches some criteria. Specifications combine with and, or and not, and the same object can select, validate and describe.

name: Normalize Unicode text
summary: Put text in one normalization form, NFC or NFD, so that the 2 ways to write a letter with an accent give the same code points.

name: Prototype pattern
summary: A program makes new objects by copying a configured example object, the prototype, and not by calling a constructor of a known class. Each class decides how deep its own copy goes.

name: Message passing
summary: In message passing, parts of a program work together by sending each other messages instead of changing shared variables. Each part owns its own state and changes it only when a message arrives.

name: Shotgun Surgery
summary: A code smell: one change to the behaviour of a program needs many small edits in many modules, and an edit that is missed is a bug.

name: Interactive debugging
summary: A debugger stops a running program at a breakpoint, runs it one step at a time, and shows its stack and variables. It controls the process through the operating system and reads debug information.

name: Mutation analysis
summary: Mutation analysis plants small faults, called mutants, in copies of a program and runs the tests on each copy. The share of mutants that make a test fail measures how well the tests find faults.

name: Push down field
summary: Move a field from a superclass into the one subclass, or the few subclasses, that use it.

name: Test-driven development
summary: Test-driven development writes a failing automated test before each piece of code, makes it pass with the least code, and then removes duplication. The cycle is red, green, refactor.

name: C#
summary: C# is a general-purpose, object-oriented language with static, strong typing and garbage collection. Programs compile to an intermediate language that the .NET runtime runs.

name: Orthogonality
summary: Keep things that are not related in concept unrelated in the system, so that a change to one does not cause a change to another.

name: State pattern
summary: An object keeps its current state in a separate state object and passes each request to it. A change of state replaces that object, so the object behaves as if its class had changed.

name: Pattern matching
summary: A pattern describes the shape of a value. A match tests a value against a list of patterns, takes the first one that fits, and binds the parts of the value to names in one step.

name: Event-driven programming
summary: Event-driven programming structures a program as handlers that an event loop calls when events happen, such as input, timers or ready sockets, so the events decide the order of work.

name: Memento pattern
summary: An object saves its internal state in a memento, an object that other code can store but cannot read. Later the object restores that state from the memento. Undo is the usual use.

name: Private class data
summary: Private class data moves the fields of a class into a separate data object that only lets them be read. Even the methods of the class cannot then change a field that was meant to be set once.

name: Replace query with parameter
summary: Move a value that a function reads from a global or another hidden source into a parameter, so that the caller supplies it.

name: Zip two lists
aliases: pair the items of two lists
loop over two lists at the same time
summary: Pair the items of two lists of integers at the same index, and stop at the end of the shorter list.

name: Composition over inheritance
summary: Composition over inheritance is the rule that a class should get behavior by holding other objects and calling them, not by extending a base class whose implementation it then depends on.

name: Constant evaluation
summary: The compiler computes the value of an expression while it translates the program, so the value can size an array, label a case or fail the build.

name: Find the length of a string
aliases: count the characters of a string
summary: Find the length of a string in UTF-8 bytes, in UTF-16 code units and in code points, and know which of them len, length, size and count give in each language.

name: Subtyping
summary: A type S is a subtype of a type T when a value of S can be used wherever a value of T is expected. Code written for T then works for every subtype, and the compiler or the runtime checks the uses.

name: Data Mapper
summary: A Data Mapper is a layer that moves data between domain objects and a database. The objects know nothing of the database, and the database knows nothing of the objects.

name: Code injection
summary: Code injection happens when a program builds code from outside input and then runs it, so the input can change what the code does.

name: Dynamic dispatch
summary: Dynamic dispatch chooses the code for a call at run time from the type of a value, usually the receiver, which lets one call site run the overriding method of each subclass.

name: Replace error code with exception
summary: Replace a special return value that signals an error with a thrown exception, in languages where exceptions are the normal way to report errors.

name: Generate random numbers
summary: Get a random integer in a range with no modulo bias, shuffle a list, repeat a sequence with a seed, and make a token with a cryptographically secure generator.

name: File system
summary: A file system keeps named files in a tree of directories on a volume. A program sees names, file types, file serial numbers and mount points, and not the blocks on the disk.

name: Singleton pattern
summary: A class makes sure that it has only one instance, and gives the whole program one global way to reach it. The global access causes most of the problems of the pattern.

name: Comment
summary: A comment is text in source code that the compiler or interpreter ignores. It holds notes for human readers, and tools can read some comments as documentation or as directives.

name: JavaScript
summary: JavaScript is a general-purpose language with dynamic, weak typing, prototype-based objects and first-class functions. ECMA-262 defines it as ECMAScript, and browsers and Node.js run it.

name: Abstract syntax tree
summary: An abstract syntax tree holds the structure of a program as a tree of operators, operands and statements. It drops the tokens that only guide the parser, such as parentheses.

name: git branch
summary: A branch is a line of development in a version control system. In Git, a branch is a name that points to one commit, and the name moves to each commit that you make on it.

name: Replace loop with pipeline
summary: Replace a loop that filters, transforms and collects items with a collection pipeline of operations such as filter, map and reduce; each language has its own form.

name: Change function declaration
summary: Change the name or the parameters of a function and update every caller, in one step when the callers are few and in stages when they are not.

name: Semantic Versioning
summary: Semantic Versioning is a set of rules for version numbers of the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. The number that changes tells the user if a release breaks the public API, adds to it or only fixes bugs.

name: Separate query from modifier
summary: Split a function that both returns a value and changes state into a query that only returns the value and a modifier that only makes the change.

name: Thread-Specific Storage
summary: Thread-Specific Storage gives each thread its own copy of an object behind one global access point. The code reads and writes the object with no lock, because no other thread can reach that copy.

name: How strings are stored
summary: A string is stored as a block of code units with a terminator or a stored length. The encoding of the units and the small string optimization change its size and speed.

name: Get a substring
summary: Get the part of a string between two indexes, know which unit each language counts, and know what happens when an index is out of range or falls inside a character.

name: Out-of-bounds write
summary: An out-of-bounds write happens when a program writes data past the end, or before the start, of a buffer, and so changes memory that belongs to other data or to the control flow of the program.

name: Sum types
summary: A value of a sum type is exactly one of a fixed set of cases, and each case carries its own data. A tag records the case, and the compiler can check that a match handles every case.

name: Get the size of a file
aliases: size of a file in bytes
summary: Get the size in bytes of a regular file from the file system, with no read of its data, and know why it is not the count of characters or the space on the disk.

name: Improper input validation
summary: Improper input validation happens when a program uses input without a correct check of the properties it needs, such as type, range and format, so values it cannot handle get through.

name: Change reference to value
aliases: replace mutation with a fresh value
summary: When a small object that is held inside another is changed in place, make it immutable: give it value equality, and replace it with a fresh object each time its contents change.

name: Bytecode
summary: Bytecode is a compact list of instructions for a virtual machine, which a program interprets one instruction at a time. A compiler produces it from the syntax tree, once, before the program runs.

name: Reverse a string
aliases: reverse the characters of a string
reverse a string by code points
reverse a string by grapheme clusters
summary: Reverse the code points of a string without breaking UTF-8 or UTF-16, and reverse its grapheme clusters where the standard library can find them.

name: Recursive descent parsing
summary: A recursive descent parser has one function for each rule of the grammar. Each function reads its tokens and calls the functions of inner rules, so the call stack follows the nesting of the input.

name: Integer overflow or wraparound
summary: An integer overflow happens when a calculation produces a value that does not fit in its integer type, so the program continues with a wrapped, truncated or undefined result that it treats as correct.

name: Constructors and initialization
summary: A constructor runs when a program creates an object and puts the object in a valid state, or refuses to create it. Languages without constructors use zero values and creation functions.

name: Partition a list
aliases: split a list by a predicate
summary: Split a list into the items that pass a test and the items that do not, here the odd and the even integers, and keep the order of the items in each part.

name: Read a CSV file
aliases: load a CSV file into records
read a CSV file with a header
summary: Read a CSV file with a header line into one record for each line, with quoted fields that hold commas, double quotes and line breaks, as RFC 4180 defines them.

name: Module pattern
summary: The module pattern groups private state and a public API in one closure or object, in a language without full support for modules. It was the usual form of a JavaScript module before ES modules.

name: Channel
summary: A channel is a typed conduit between concurrent processes. One process sends a value into it and another receives the value, so the two exchange data and synchronize without shared variables.

name: Grapheme cluster
summary: A grapheme cluster is what a user sees as one character, such as é, a flag or a family emoji. It can be many code points, and UAX 29 gives the rules that find its boundaries.

name: Array programming
summary: Array programming treats a whole array as one value, so operations such as + and max apply to every element at once, and reductions, scans and outer products replace explicit loops.

name: Async/await
summary: An async function can pause at each await until a result is ready, and a scheduler runs other tasks in the meantime. Code that waits for many things reads like sequential code.

name: git commit
summary: A commit is a saved snapshot of the whole project, with an author, a date, a message and links to its parent commits. Git names each commit by the hash of its bytes.

name: Temporary Field
summary: A code smell: an object has fields that hold a value only in some cases or during one computation, so a reader cannot tell when the field is valid and the code must check it each time.

name: Half-Sync/Half-Async
summary: Half-Sync/Half-Async splits a concurrent system into layers. Short handlers react to events and never block, threads run the long tasks with blocking calls, and a queue joins the two layers.

name: Proactor
summary: A proactor starts asynchronous operations and, when each one completes, calls its completion handler, so the program reacts to finished work and not to readiness.

name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
summary: A code smell: two classes do the same job but have different method names and parameters, so a client cannot swap one for the other and must know which one it has.

name: Sync a file to disk
summary: Write a file and do not return until its data is on the storage device, with fsync on the file and then on its directory, so that the data and the name stay after a crash or a power loss.

name: Repository pattern
summary: A repository gives the domain code a collection-like interface to stored objects, such as add, get and find by criteria, and hides the database queries and the mapping behind it.

name: Side effect
summary: A side effect is a change that a function makes beyond its return value, such as a write to a variable, a file or the screen. It makes the order and the number of calls matter.

name: Get the code point of a character
summary: Get the number of the code point of a character, not the value of its first byte or its first UTF-16 code unit.

name: Immutable object
summary: An immutable object cannot change after its constructor ends. Threads can share it and read it with no lock, and an update makes a new object instead of a change to the shared one.

name: Binding
summary: A binding is the link between a name and the thing that it names, such as a value, a storage location or a function. Rebinding a name is a different thing from changing the object it names.

name: Program state
summary: The state of a running program is everything it remembers at one moment: the values of its variables and objects, the place it has reached in the code, and its open files.

name: Reactive programming
summary: Reactive programming states how values depend on each other, as cells in a spreadsheet do, and a runtime updates the dependent values or streams when their inputs change.

name: Change value to reference
aliases: use a repository for shared objects
summary: When many copies of one logical object exist, and an update to it must be seen by all holders, keep one shared object for it in a repository, and give each holder a reference to that object.

name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
summary: A code smell: two class hierarchies mirror each other, so each subclass added to one needs a matching subclass in the other, and the two must change together.

name: Convert a string to bytes
summary: Get the bytes of a string in UTF-8, and give the encoding each time so that the result does not change with the platform.

name: Interpreter pattern
summary: Represent each rule of a small language as a class, build a tree of those objects for a sentence, and evaluate the sentence by asking the root of the tree to interpret itself.

name: Replace type code with subclasses
summary: Replace a field that holds a type code, such as "engineer" or "salesman", with one subclass for each value of the code.

name: Inline variable
summary: Replace the uses of a local variable with the expression that it holds, then delete the variable, when the name says no more than the expression.

name: What a program is
summary: A program is text in a programming language that describes a computation. A run of it reads input, changes state step by step, writes output and ends with an exit status.

name: TOML
summary: TOML is a text format for configuration files. A TOML document is one table of key and value pairs, with strings, integers, floats, booleans, four date and time types, arrays and nested tables.

name: Template Method pattern
summary: A base class method fixes the steps of an algorithm and calls other methods for the steps that vary. Subclasses override those steps and leave the order of the steps alone.

name: Producer-consumer
summary: Producers put items into a shared buffer and consumers take them out. A bounded buffer makes a producer wait when it is full and a consumer wait when it is empty, so neither side runs too far ahead.

name: Just-in-time compilation
summary: Just-in-time compilation translates code after the program starts. A runtime interprets first, counts calls, and compiles hot code for the types it saw, with guards that fall back.

name: Formal semantics
summary: A formal semantics gives programs an exact meaning in mathematics: as steps of a machine, as functions, or as rules for proofs. Tools use it to prove facts about programs.

name: C
summary: C is a general-purpose, compiled language for system programming, with static, weak typing, pointers and manual memory management. The standard ISO/IEC 9899 defines it.

name: Law of Demeter
summary: A method should call only the methods of objects it knows directly, its own object, its parameters, the objects it creates and its fields, and not reach through them to objects further away.

name: Cross-site request forgery
summary: Cross-site request forgery happens when a web application trusts a request because it carries the user's cookies, so a page on another site can make the browser act for the user.

name: Incomplete Library Class
summary: A code smell: a class from a library lacks a method that the program needs, the library cannot be changed, and the missing code is written again in each place that needs it.

name: Iterator pattern
summary: An iterator object gives the elements of a collection one at a time and keeps the position, so a client can walk any collection without knowing how it stores them.

name: Property-based testing
summary: A property-based test states a rule that must hold for all inputs of a kind. A tool generates many inputs, checks the rule on each, and shrinks a failing input to a small one.

name: Order of evaluation
summary: The order of evaluation decides when each operand, argument and side effect of an expression happens. Some languages fix it from left to right, and C and C++ leave most of it open.

name: Replace temp with query
summary: Replace a local variable that holds a computed value with a function that computes it, so that other functions can ask for the value and the long function gets easier to split.

name: Read an environment variable
aliases: read an env var with a default
summary: Read one environment variable of the process, return the value also when it is empty, and return a default only when the variable is not set.

name: String indexing
summary: An index into a string counts bytes, UTF-16 code units or code points, and the choice decides the cost of s[i] and whether a slice can cut a character in half.

name: Parse an integer
aliases: convert a string to an integer
parse a number from a string
read an integer in a given base
summary: Parse a string as a signed 64-bit integer in a base from 2 to 36, with a strict syntax, and report bad text and a value out of range as two different errors.

name: Replace inline code with function call
summary: Replace inline code that does what an existing function already does with a call to that function, from the project or from a library, so that the code says what it does by name.

name: Search a sorted list
summary: Find the first index of a value in a sorted list of integers with a binary search, or give -1 when the value is not in the list.

name: Immutability
summary: An immutable value cannot change after the program makes it. A program that needs a different value makes a fresh one, so every holder of the value sees the same state.

name: Servant
summary: A servant is a class that gives one behaviour to a group of classes. The served objects implement a small interface, and the servant takes them as parameters.

name: Twin
summary: The Twin pattern models multiple inheritance in a language that has only single inheritance. Two linked objects each inherit from one parent, and together they act as one object.

name: Adapter pattern
summary: An adapter converts the interface of an existing class into the interface that a client expects. The client and the class stay as they are, and the adapter translates each call.

name: Whole-Part
summary: The Whole-Part pattern aggregates components that form a semantic unit. The whole encapsulates its parts, organizes their collaboration, and gives clients one interface to them.

name: Defer and finally
summary: Cleanup constructs run code when control leaves a scope, on every path out: the normal end, a return, a break or an exception. Programs use them to close files, release locks and undo partial work.

name: Garbage collection
summary: Garbage collection frees the memory of objects that the program can no longer reach. The program allocates objects but never frees them, and the runtime finds the dead ones.

name: Serialization
summary: Serialization turns values in memory into bytes or text that a file or a network can carry, and deserialization rebuilds the values. The format decides what survives the trip.

name: Iterator
summary: An iterator gives the elements of a sequence one at a time and remembers its position between calls. A loop asks it for the next element until it says that no elements are left.

name: Comments
summary: A code smell, not the practice of writing comments: a comment explains what unclear code does, where clearer code would not need the comment.

name: Data race
summary: A data race is two accesses to one memory location from different threads, at least one a write, with no synchronization that orders them. In C and C++ it is undefined behaviour.

name: Type erasure
summary: Type erasure removes type information when a program is compiled. Reification keeps it for the run time. Java and TypeScript erase type arguments, and C# and Go keep them.

name: Remove characters from a string
summary: Remove each character of a set from a string, and remove whole code points, not bytes or UTF-16 code units.

name: Hard-coded credentials
summary: Hard-coded credentials are passwords, keys or tokens written into the source code or the binary of a program, where everyone who can read the code or the history can read them.

name: Concatenate strings
summary: Join two strings into one with the operator or function of each language, and know the rules when one operand is a number or null and the cost of repeated concatenation.

name: Fork/Join
summary: Fork/Join splits a task into parts that can run in parallel, and then joins them, so that only one thread continues with the combined result. Recursive splitting gives parallel divide and conquer.

name: Characters, code points and graphemes
summary: Text has four layers. Readers see grapheme clusters, Unicode numbers code points, an encoding stores them as code units, and the units become bytes. Each language counts one layer.

name: Keep it simple
summary: Make simplicity a design goal: choose the simplest design that does the job, and add complexity only when the job needs it.

name: Large Class
summary: A code smell: a class has too many fields, too many methods or too much code, because it does several jobs, and each change to one job must be made among the parts of the others.

name: Inversion of control
summary: A framework, not the program, holds the main flow of control and calls the code that the program plugs into it; it is a defining feature of a framework, as opposed to a library.

name: Introduce parameter object
summary: Replace a group of parameters that travel together with one object that holds them, so that the group has a name and a place for the behaviour that belongs to it.

name: git merge
summary: A merge joins two lines of development. Git compares both tips with their merge base, keeps the changes of each side, and records the result as a commit with two parents.

name: Uncontrolled resource consumption
aliases: denial of service by resource exhaustion
summary: Uncontrolled resource consumption happens when input decides how much memory, time, stack or other resource a program uses, with no limit, so that one request can starve the others.

name: Double dispatch
summary: Double dispatch selects a method by the run-time types of two objects. In a single-dispatch language, the first call dispatches on the receiver, and it calls back the argument, which dispatches again.

name: Truncate a file
aliases: set the size of a file
extend a file with zero bytes
summary: Set the size of an existing file to a given number of bytes. Cut the bytes after the new end, or add zero bytes up to it, and do not make a file when none is there.

name: Delete a file
aliases: delete a file if it exists
summary: Delete the file at a path and tell whether a file was there, with no error for a missing file but an error for a directory and for each other failure, such as a permission error.

name: Hard links and symbolic links
summary: A hard link is one more name for the same file, and the file stays while one name is left. A symbolic link is a small file that holds a path, which the system follows, so it can dangle or loop.

name: Reactor
summary: A reactor waits for events on many handles in one thread and calls the handler that is registered for each handle, so one thread serves many connections.

name: Numeric type
summary: A numeric type holds numbers of one kind, such as integers, floating-point numbers, decimals or complex numbers. Its range, its precision and its rules for division and mixing differ by language.

name: Pointers and references
summary: A reference is a value that leads to another value, so several parts of a program can share one object without copies. A pointer is a reference that holds a memory address.

name: Annotations
summary: Structured metadata attached to declarations in source code, such as @Override in Java or #[derive] in Rust, which a compiler, a tool or the running program reads.

name: Split a string
aliases: split a string on a delimiter
summary: Split a string into fields on a literal separator, keep the empty fields, stop after a limit, and also split on white space and on a regular expression.

name: Parameter passing
summary: Parameter passing is how the arguments of a call reach the parameters of a function: as copies, as references to variables, as shared objects or as unevaluated expressions.

name: Panic
summary: A panic is how a program reacts to a bug that it finds while it runs. It stops the current work, and either ends the process or lets a boundary throw the broken work away.

name: Sort a list of records
summary: Sort a list of records by one field, then by a second field in the opposite direction, with a stable sort so that records with equal keys keep their input order.

name: Git
summary: Git is a distributed version control system. Each clone holds the full history of a project, and Git stores that history as snapshots that are named by their hashes.

name: Find the largest element
summary: Find the largest item of a non-empty list of integers, and know what each language does for an empty list.

name: Fuzz testing
summary: Fuzz testing runs a program on a large number of generated or mutated inputs and watches for crashes, hangs and failed checks. Coverage-guided fuzzers keep the inputs that reach unseen code.

name: CSV
summary: CSV is a text format for a table. Each line is a record, commas separate the fields, and double quotes enclose a field that holds a comma, a quote or a line break.

name: Null Object
summary: A null object has the same interface as a real collaborator but does nothing. A client can use it in place of null, so the client needs no checks for null.

name: Replace conditional with polymorphism
summary: When a switch on a type code is repeated in several functions, make a class for each case and move each branch into a method of its class, so that the call dispatches to the right code with no switch.

name: Reduce a list to a value
summary: Combine the items of a list into one value with an accumulator, here the sum of a list of integers, and give an initial value for the empty list.

name: Remove setting method
summary: Remove the setter of a field that must not change after the object is made, and set the field once, in the constructor.

name: Slide statements
summary: Move statements up or down so that code that works on the same thing is together, after checking that the move does not change what the code does; a usual first step before Extract Function.

name: Functional programming
summary: Functional programming builds a program from pure functions and values that do not change, and joins small functions into larger ones with higher-order functions and composition.

name: Append to a file
aliases: append a line to a file
add text to the end of a file
summary: Add one line to the end of a file in append mode, with one write call, so that many threads or processes can add lines to the same file and no line overwrites another.

name: Tree-walking interpreter
summary: A tree-walking interpreter runs a program by visiting the nodes of its syntax tree. It evaluates the children of each node first, and keeps the values of variables in a chain of environments.

name: Error value
summary: An error value is an ordinary value that a function returns to say that it failed. The caller tests the value and decides what to do next, so the path of each failure is visible in the code.

name: File metadata
summary: File metadata is the data about a file that is not in its bytes: the type, the size, the owner, the permissions, the link count and the times. A stat call reads it, with or without a link.

name: YAML
summary: YAML is a text format for data that uses indentation to show structure. Its nodes are scalars, sequences and mappings. A schema decides if an unquoted scalar is a string, a number, a boolean or null.

name: Replace superclass with delegate
summary: Replace inheritance from a class whose interface does not fit the subclass with a field that holds an instance of that class, and forward only the calls that are needed.

name: Imperative programming
summary: Imperative programming describes a computation as a sequence of statements that change the values of variables, so the program states the steps that lead to the result.

name: Object-oriented programming
summary: Object-oriented programming builds a program from objects that keep private state and answer method calls, so code can ask an object to act without knowing its exact kind.

name: Separation of mechanism and policy
summary: Keep the code that does a job (the mechanism) apart from the code that decides how the job is used (the policy), so that the policy can change without a change to the mechanism.

name: Watch a file for changes
summary: Tell when a file is created, changed or deleted, by polling its size and modification time or by an event API of the operating system, and act once for each burst of changes.

name: Combine functions into class
summary: Turn a group of functions that all take the same data into a class that holds the data, so that the shared context is explicit and the calls get shorter.

name: Decompose conditional
summary: When an if statement has a long condition and long branches, extract the condition and each branch into a function with a name that says what it means, so that the if statement reads as the rule.

name: Write a file
aliases: write a string to a file
summary: Write a string to a file as UTF-8 with no change to its bytes, in one of three modes, truncate, append, or atomic replacement through a temporary file in the same directory.

name: Design principle
summary: A general rule that guides the choices of a design, such as how to divide a program into parts and what each part may know about the others.

name: Robustness principle
aliases: be conservative in what you send
be liberal in what you accept
summary: Send only what the specification allows, and accept any input whose meaning is clear; a guideline from early Internet protocols that later work says can make protocols less robust over time.

name: Replace constructor with factory function
summary: Replace direct calls of a constructor with calls of an ordinary function that makes the object, so that the creation can have a name and can choose what to return.

name: Missing authentication for a critical function
summary: Missing authentication happens when a function that needs a known user, such as an admin endpoint or a debug port, accepts requests from anyone who can reach it.

name: Facade pattern
summary: One object or module gives a single, higher-level interface to a subsystem of many classes. Clients call the facade, and the facade calls the subsystem in the right order.

name: Deadlock
summary: A deadlock is a cycle of waits. Each thread in the cycle holds a resource and waits for a resource that the next thread holds, so no thread in the cycle can continue.

name: Replace subclass with delegate
summary: Replace a subclass that holds one variation of behavior with a separate delegate object that the main class holds and calls.

name: CPU profiling
summary: A CPU profiler measures where a running program spends its processor time. It samples the call stack at intervals or counts each call, and reports the result per function or per path.

name: Data Class
summary: A code smell: a class has fields and accessors and no behaviour, while the rules about its data live in the classes that use it, often copied in several places.

name: Dead code
summary: A code smell: the source has functions that nobody calls, branches that cannot run and values that nobody reads, and each reader must still read them and keep them working.

name: Introduce special case
summary: When many callers check for the same special value, such as a missing customer, and then do the same thing, make an object for the special case that gives that behavior, and remove the checks.

name: Parse and format a date
summary: Parse an RFC 3339 date-time with a UTC offset, reject text that is not valid, and print the same instant in UTC with exactly three fraction digits.

name: Deserialization of untrusted data
summary: Deserialization of untrusted data happens when a program rebuilds objects from bytes that an attacker controls, in a format that lets the bytes choose the classes to create or the code to run.

name: Read from standard input
summary: Read the standard input of the process to the end of input, line by line, and return each line without its newline or CRLF.

name: Control flow
summary: Control flow is the order in which a program runs its statements. Sequence, selection, iteration, jumps, calls and exceptions are the ways to change that order.

name: Simple design
summary: Kent Beck's four rules for a simple design, in priority order: the code passes the tests, reveals intention, has no duplication, and has the fewest elements.

name: Value
summary: A value is a piece of data that a program computes with, such as 42, "hi" or a list. Expressions give values, variables hold them, and functions take and return them.

name: Retry with backoff
summary: A retry calls a failed operation again, in case the failure was temporary. Backoff makes each wait longer, and jitter makes it random, so that retries do not overload the service that failed.

name: Multiton
summary: A multiton keeps one instance of a class for each key. A static method returns the instance for a key, creates it on the first request and returns the same object later.

name: Downcasting
summary: A code smell: code tests the run-time class of an object and casts it to a subclass to reach what it needs, because the type it was given does not offer that operation.

name: JSON
summary: JSON is a text format for structured data, based on the object and array literals of JavaScript. A value is an object, an array, a string, a number, true, false or null.

name: Get the modification time of a file
summary: Get the time of the last change to the data of a file as Unix time in whole seconds, and know how it differs from the change, access and creation times.

name: Push down method
summary: Move a method from a superclass into the one subclass, or the few subclasses, that use it.

name: Creational pattern
summary: A creational pattern is a design pattern for the creation of objects. It hides which concrete classes a program uses and how their instances are created and combined.

name: Integer representation
summary: An integer type stores whole numbers in a fixed number of bits. Unsigned types read the bits as a binary number, and almost all machines store signed values in two's complement.

name: Iterate over the characters of a string
summary: Visit each code point of a string in order, not each byte or each UTF-16 code unit.

name: Lock a file
summary: Take a shared or an exclusive advisory lock on a whole file without a wait, so that programs which use the same lock do not change the file at the same time, and release it when the work is done.

name: Concurrency pattern
summary: A concurrency pattern is a design pattern for work that runs at the same time. Each one answers the same question: which code may touch which state, and when.

name: Finite-state machines
summary: A finite-state machine is always in one of a fixed set of states and moves between them on each input symbol. Regular expressions, lexers and network protocols are such machines.

name: Reversibility
summary: Make design decisions in a way that lets you change them later at low cost, or put them off until you have more information, because irreversible decisions are a main source of complexity.

name: Declaration
summary: A declaration introduces a name and tells the compiler what the name is, such as a variable of a type or a function with a signature. A definition is a declaration that also gives the thing itself.

name: Replace primitive with object
summary: Wrap a string or a number that stands for a concept of the domain, such as an email address or an amount of money, in a small class that holds the rules of that concept.

name: Return modified value
summary: Change a function that updates a variable outside itself so that it computes the value and returns it, and let the caller assign the result.
